citations.quote: Near-IR Spectrometry (includes FTIR, NIR-IR, or diffraction grating/slit spectrometer, Diffuse Reflection fiber probe, or Transmission fiber probe) Near-IR vibrational spectroscopy (NIR) is the most common online analysis method performed using fiber optic probes.
ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples, such as biological tissue, using specialized probes utilizing high-transmission fiber optics in the Mid-IR region.
Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000–400 cm-1) is one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis.

risks: Probe fouling or material buildup on the window at high temperature
Incorrect method choice if melt is opaque and a transmission probe is selected

steps: Collect melt samples at relevant temperatures and prepare them in lab cuvettes or small flow cells.
Measure with candidate techniques (NIR transmission, NIR diffuse reflection, Raman) while recording a reference assay (e.g., HPLC) for the target variable.
Build chemometric models (calibration or classification) using the spectra and reference data.
Validate on held‑out melt batches to assess prediction error.
Select the method that meets the required accuracy and can be implemented with a probe compatible with the temperature and fouling conditions.
Then measure in-line or in a pilot set-up against the reference method.
feasibility.decisionBasis: Comparison of model performance (RMSEP, bias) against acceptance criteria agreed with the customer; the simplest method that meets the criteria will be chosen. Agree two things separately with the customer before the test: the model accuracy required against the reference method, and the alarm or action threshold applied to the measured value.
